question: A 65-year-old man presents with acute abdominal pain accompanied by chills, nausea, and vomiting. His past medical history is significant for benign prostatic hyperplasia and diabetes mellitus type 2. His medications are tamsulosin and metformin. His last HbA1c, 5 months ago, was 6.7. He had a screening colonoscopy 5 years ago which was normal. He denies blood in the stool or urine and has had no change in bowel habits. Throughout the encounter, the patient has difficulty getting comfortable on the exam table. His temperature is 38.2°C (100.7°F), the heart rate is 103/min, the respiratory rate is 15/min, and the blood pressure is 105/85 mm Hg. Physical exam is significant for left costovertebral angle tenderness. Peritoneal signs are absent. CBC, CMP, and urinalysis results are pending. Abdominal X-ray is shown. Which of the following is the next best step in management?

options.opa: Observation with hydration, bed rest, and analgesics

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "65-year-old man" -> "presents with acute abdominal pain, chills, nausea, vomiting" -> "significant for benign prostatic hyperplasia, diabetes mellitus type 2" -> "medications: tamsulosin, metformin" -> "last HbA1c 6.7 five months ago" -> "screening colonoscopy 5 years ago normal" -> "denies blood in stool or urine, no change in bowel habits" -> "difficulty getting comfortable on exam table" -> "temperature 38.2°C, heart rate 103/min, respiratory rate 15/min, BP 105/85 mm Hg" -> "left costovertebral angle tenderness" -> "Peritoneal signs absent" -> "CBC, CMP, urinalysis pending" -> "Abdominal X-ray shown" -> "Next best step in management?" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Abdominal X-ray findings" -> "suggestive of kidney stone or urinary tract infection" -> "consideration for urinary tract infection" -> "management options: observation with hydration, bed rest, analgesics; amlodipine; antibiotics; surgical removal and antibiotics; urine alkalinization" -> "evaluate further based on lab results" -> 80%
analysis: The patient's presentation with acute abdominal pain, chills, nausea, vomiting, fever, and left costovertebral angle tenderness raises concern for acute pyelonephritis, especially given his history of diabetes and benign prostatic hyperplasia. The next best step in management would be to start antibiotics to treat the likely underlying infection.
